realism_constraints: No modern forensic DNA analysis or electronic surveillance
Medical and police procedures based on physical evidence and witness testimony
Communication and travel limited to pre-digital means, e.g. letters, telegrams, trams
location: London, England, including Highgate, Hornsey, Hoxton, and Inner Temple
institution: Criminal Investigation Department (C.I.D.) and Dr. John Thorndyke's private investigation
crime_subtype: fraudulent death and identity substitution by wax mask

cast.name: Stephen Gray
cast.motive_seed: friendship and justice for Marion D’Arblay

cast.name: Julius D’Arblay
cast.private_secret: made wax mask used in fraud

cast.name: Mr. Simon Bendelow (alias Morris)
cast.private_secret: murderer, faked death using wax mask

surface_summary: Julius D’Arblay is found dead in a pond, apparently drowned, but later discovered to have been murdered by aconitine poisoning via hypodermic injection. Suspicion falls on a mysterious man connected to a stolen unique coin and a wax mask. The investigation reveals a complex plot involving faked deaths, identity substitution, and a criminal masquerading as the deceased.
accepted_facts: Julius D’Arblay was murdered by aconitine poisoning administered with a hypodermic syringe.
Simon Bendelow was believed dead but was actually alive and faked his death using a wax mask.
The unique electrotype coin found in the pond was made by Julius D’Arblay.
The cremation of Bendelow was a fraud involving a wax mask and an empty coffin.
inferred_conclusions: The man who attacked Marion D’Arblay was not the murderer but an unrelated assailant.
The death certificates and funerals of Bendelow and Crile were legitimate and truthful.
The police had correctly identified Bendelow and Crile as dead and unrelated to the ongoing threat.
mechanism_description: Simon Bendelow, a professional criminal, faked his death by commissioning Julius D’Arblay to make a wax mask of his face. After murdering D’Arblay to silence him, Bendelow substituted the wax mask over a corpse in a coffin with an inspection window and staged a cremation to create false evidence of his death. He then lived under an alias, continuing his criminal activities until Thorndyke’s investigation uncovered the deception and led to his arrest.
delivery_path: Bendelow commissions D’Arblay to make a wax mask of his face.
Bendelow murders D’Arblay to prevent exposure of the mask.
Bendelow substitutes the wax mask over a corpse in a coffin with an inspection window.
The coffin is presented to witnesses and cremated to fake Bendelow’s death.
Bendelow assumes a new identity and continues criminal activities.
Thorndyke discovers the wax mask and connects it to Bendelow.
Police arrest Bendelow after coordinated surveillance and evidence gathering.
outcome_result: Simon Bendelow is arrested and exposed as the murderer and fraudster behind the elaborate deception.

false_assumption.statement: The two men, Bendelow and Crile, were both dead and buried as stated in official records.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Death certificates and funerals were officially recorded and witnessed by multiple parties, including doctors and acquaintances. The presence of cremation and burial records provides strong documentary evidence supporting their deaths.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: One of the men, Bendelow, faked his death using a wax mask and an empty coffin, allowing him to evade capture and continue his criminal activities.

supporting_points: Morris was identified by a plaster mask found at the studio.
He was seen following Dr. Gray and was suspected of suspicious activities.
His shop contained unusual and decayed antiques suggesting illicit dealings.
He was connected to the victim through the wax mask.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Morris was actually Simon Bendelow in disguise, using the alias to conceal his identity.

red_herrings.description: The deliberate cutting of Marion D’Arblay’s bicycle brake wire suggested a malicious attempt on her life.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: An unknown local saboteur or mentally defective adult
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The act was a crude attempt by the murderer to intimidate or harm Marion but was not directly linked to the murder itself.

red_herrings.description: The falling derrick on the canal tow-path that caused Dr. Gray to fall into the water appeared to be an accident or sabotage.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Mr. Morris or an unknown assailant near the canal
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The derrick fell due to a poorly secured rope slipping off the cleat, likely accidental rather than intentional sabotage.

closed_circle.rationale: The suspects are limited to those with direct connection to the victim, the wax mask, and the forged death, all residing or operating within the London area and connected through the investigation.

time_anchors: Death of Julius D’Arblay on the morning found
Death of Bendelow and Crile within days of each other
Time of attempted murder on Marion D’Arblay
time_windows: Periods of surveillance and watch over Marion
Times of police stakeouts and arrests
access_objects: Morris’ house with two street frontages
trust_channels: Witness testimony of spinsters and family

inference_path.observation: The body found in the pond had a needle puncture in the back and died of aconitine poisoning.
inference_path.correction: Death was homicide, not drowning or suicide.
inference_path.effect: The case is murder, not accident or natural causes.
required_evidence: Medical witness testimony at the inquest

inference_path.observation: An ancient coin found in the pond was an electrotype made by Julius D’Arblay.
inference_path.correction: The coin links the victim to a forgery operation.
inference_path.effect: Motive may involve fraudulent coin production.

inference_path.observation: Simon Bendelow was declared dead and cremated, but the coffin was later found empty.
inference_path.correction: Bendelow faked his death using a wax mask and an empty coffin.
inference_path.effect: Bendelow is alive and the prime suspect.
required_evidence: Wax mask found in D’Arblay’s studio

inference_path.observation: Two elderly spinsters identified the wax mask as Bendelow’s face.
inference_path.correction: The mask was used to fake Bendelow’s death.
inference_path.effect: Confirms the identity of the wax mask and the deception.
required_evidence: Interview with Miss Dewsnep and Miss Bonington

inference_path.observation: Marion D’Arblay was attacked by a man matching the description of Morris.
inference_path.correction: Morris is actually Bendelow in disguise using make-up and a wax mask.
inference_path.effect: The attacker and murderer are the same person.

inference_path.observation: The murder victim’s studio was ransacked and a plaster mould was broken.
inference_path.correction: The murderer searched for the wax mask mould to destroy evidence.
inference_path.effect: Motive for murder was to conceal the fraudulent death.
required_evidence: List of missing or disturbed moulds

inference_path.observation: The police arrested a man with a red nose and different appearance than expected.
inference_path.correction: The arrested man was the disguised Bendelow using make-up and a wax mask.
inference_path.effect: The true murderer was caught despite disguise.

discriminating_test.design: A wax mask was made from the plaster mould of Morris’ face and altered with clay to resemble the assailant’s description. A photograph was taken and shown to the witnesses to test recognition without suggestion. The mask was also used in a coffin with an inspection window to simulate Bendelow’s death.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test revealed that the assailant was indeed Morris (Bendelow) disguised with make-up and that the wax mask was used to fake the cremation death.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Witnesses must positively identify the wax mask as the face of the assailant and Bendelow, confirming the deception.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the characters, the wax masks, the unique coin, and the suspicious circumstances surrounding the deaths and cremation. The clues about the wax mask’s existence, the forged coin, and the suspicious behavior of Morris are all presented openly. The reader could deduce the use of a wax mask to fake Bendelow’s death and the motive for murdering D’Arblay to conceal the fraud.
